findings.title: Limits of this verdict
findings.evidence: One run per cell; sections with <= 15 frames flip between pass and fail (1024 principles 13 frames here vs 59 in r2; 1440 kill-list 13). The pop detector skips frames where scroll moved >= 40 px, so Lenis runs under-count pops. No P3-0 run at 1024. The 'alt' run is not defined in the J8 inputs (treated as a second Lenis run). 4.4 rows needing the intro trace were not re-measured (#intro repaints, hand-off script, name frame, media state). The reader and skimmer recordings never wheel-scroll inside the 3 s after quiet-end. Nothing here shows real-GPU behaviour.

recommendations.action: Make sure no idle-time job can hold the main thread for more than about 50 ms, and keep all of it away from the play screen and from the first 2,000 px of scroll: run it in small slices, yield to input, and start only after the intro has ended and the visitor has stopped scrolling for a moment.
recommendations.why: The only app-owned long task in the data (100-1,013 ms), and it lands on the two moments that set the first impression: Play and the first scroll. It is the worst clip of skimmer-1440 and an outlier in all five recordings.
recommendations.check: Re-capture: no LoAF with >= 50 ms of work on the play screen or at y < 2,000 in any recording; clips #19 / #18 / #10 / #6 / #11 stop being outliers; intro play-screen script < 100 ms.

recommendations.action: Bring layout shift to exactly 0: reserve the space of the films-section block that moves at about 33 s (it also moves under reduced motion), make caption lines keep their size when the per-world face arrives (fallback with matched metrics, or have the face ready before the caption enters), and split the scrubbed words before first paint in beyond.
recommendations.why: Spec says 0; r3 is 0.0454 at 1440 (r2 0.006) and non-zero in 9 of 12 runs. These are deterministic, so they are real regardless of the GPU.
recommendations.check: CLS 0 in desktop, native, alt, gl and rm at both widths.

recommendations.action: Make the reveal a pure compositor wipe and the name an on-time fade: do the heavy preparation during the hold, with no script in the last half second before the reveal; show the name on the second reveal frame by fading opacity, never appearing in one step. If the titles design deliberately sequences caption then name, change section 4.4's wording to match.
recommendations.why: The single biggest visible hitch (731 ms at 1440), the one-frame name pop at both widths, and a 76 / 112 ms script task at hold are all in the first 10 seconds.
recommendations.check: Intro trace: reveal-frame max < 100 ms headless; name present on frame 2, no pop in the strip; no task > 10 ms between hold and reveal.

recommendations.action: Cut principles to at most 8 promoted layers and remove or flatten the large xl-only block that costs raster even with motion off.
recommendations.why: Worst section in 4 of 5 recordings; rm at 1440 is 31.5 fps against 60 everywhere else; 12 / 11 layers against the budget of 8.
recommendations.check: rm principles >= 55 fps at 1440; desktop principles >= 4.95 at 1024 on at least 40 frames; skimmer/reader principles no longer the lowest-fps section.

recommendations.action: Lighten the first scroll and the last card. Act-1: fewer large images and masks in view at once. Act-4 (and act-3 / voices): the 21 and 9 infinite animations pause while a card transition is running and whenever they are off screen.
recommendations.why: Act-1 and act-4 are the sections that got 3-4x slower than P3-0 (28.8 -> 7.7, 38.0 -> 12.6 fps); act-1 is where every visitor starts scrolling.
recommendations.check: act-1 and act-4 card transitions back above P3-0's 26 / 29 fps on the Lenis path, or at least above 15.

recommendations.action: Find out why the journey section is not producing frames at rest (0.3 / 0.6 fps) and why act-4 at 1440 keeps repainting its card shape at rest; then make rest truly still: only a visible loop may run.
recommendations.why: P3-0 idled at 60 fps in both. Something is looping or stalled, and it is a defect on a real GPU too.
recommendations.check: Idle probe: every section >= 55 fps at both widths, hero excepted until a real-GPU read.

recommendations.action: Calm the journey seam push (B12) and the journey opening (B09): make the push cheaper, or shorten it, so that it holds frames in the relative measure.
recommendations.why: Worst or near-worst clip in 4-5 of 5 recordings at 416-500 ms per frame; also the drift #2 failure at 1024 and the only 2+ stars clips.
recommendations.check: Clips for B12 / B09 no longer in each run's worst ten; drift #2 >= .95 at 1024.

recommendations.action: Stop plate cameras, stage layers and cards from re-rasterising on every scroll frame: movement by transform and opacity only, and no filters, masks or blends on anything that moves.
recommendations.why: Act-card-stage, stage-cam, plate-cam and campSticky repaint in 73-100 % of paints; raster during scroll is about 290-980 ms/s against about 0 at rest; raster-diet items 2, 3, 4, 6 and 8 are not shown fixed.
recommendations.check: Repaint-node list shows <= 2 repaints per card transition; will-change and filter counts match the diet table.

recommendations.action: Aryan's real-GPU pass on the laptop is now the deciding measure; ask for it on these five moments: the first scroll through act-1, journey B12, principles, kill-list and the intro reveal, plus a fast fling, with the Media panel open for the hardware decoder.
recommendations.why: The raster-bound misses (skimmer 8.6 fps, intro fps, INP 544 ms) may disappear on a GPU, or may not; headless cannot say. Until then the score carries about a point of uncertainty either way.
recommendations.check: Spec 12.1 real-GPU row: p95 <= 20 ms, <= 2 % of frames > 33 ms, none > 50 ms in cards, idle 60 fps.

recommendations.action: Tighten the measurement for the next round: three motion.js runs per width with the spread reported; the intro trace so the four 4.4 rows are measured; LoAFs tagged by work >= 50 ms next to the duration count; a P3-0-style baseline at 1024; define the 'alt' run in the manifest; and let the pop detector see continuously moving frames.
recommendations.why: Several verdict rows rest on 13-19 frames and one run, and four 4.4 rows are unmeasured.
recommendations.check: Each headline row carries a spread and a frame count.
